questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Sun, different culture, inside EU, a destination I have not visited before

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only rate the stay 6 out of ten due to the fact I was promised the course "Private international Law" was in English, but as it turned out I had to learn Spanish laws and regulation, which was not mentioned anywhere. I was referred to use Google Translate, which is very unprofessional in my opinion. So, I ended op with only 25 ETCS points, even though I needed 30 ETCS points.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The Host university did not help at all - you were left on your own and was very difficult to get help no matter the issue. 

Further, I received a course which had Spanish laws and legislation, even though the University promised everything was in English. There were no mentions of Spanish legislation or laws in the course description and the course was categorized as an English course. The teacher and university said I should use google translate or deepl. I do not speak Spanish and I didn't even attend the intensive course at the university. At the end I had to drop the class because of the Spanish parts - it is very criticizable.
I was en contact with Eva (the person responsible for exchange students) through many months leading up to the exchange. I told her many times, that I do not speak English, and that it is very important that I receive English courses. She guaranteed that courses categorized as English also where 100% in English - this turned out to be false.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
None. 
The first day of school there was an introduction, however, I was told I shouldn't go because there was also a class at the same time. So I did not receive any assistance, and I was actually not sure when I was even supposed to show up at school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was somewhat easy. In my experience you should start at least 4 month in advance. 1,5 month before almost everything is gone. 
I used Badi - I can recommend the website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I heard a lot of people got scammed when doing student housing, so they never received their deposit back. 
Poble Sec is a very nice area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit difficult to know which courses were available and to get information about the courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online bidding system - first come, first served system. It worked pretty well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The online help available was through Eva (the one in charge of students abroad) she was not very helpful. She couldn't gaurantee wether I could get 30 ECTS credit points. (which is a condition from my home university) and she did not do anything to try and help my situation. And the end I had to take a chance because she did not provide much information. I ended up getting 30 ETCS credits in English courses - however, one of the courses ended up containing Spanish legislation and laws, even though Eva, the available information nor the Uni never ever mentioned that, so I had to drop the course and ended up with only 25 ETC points.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succsessful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you receive an update course discription.... Only take courses former exchange students has had.
Just because a course is categorized as English, does not mean it is 100% English - do research on the course  yourself, becouse you can not trust the information you get from the University.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly, I did not learn a lot..

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The teachers could do what ever they wanted in their classes, so a lot of the time the syllabus was not teached, and they changed the syllabus through out the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. At UCPH the syllabus and learning objectives are somewhat determined by the government, and therefore you know exactly what is expected of you and what you have to know to be able to pass an exam. At Esade, you never really knew what was expected and the syllabus and learning objectives was not really followed. Further, in several classes there was not homework, readings or anything - what you had to know was mentioned ONCE in class and if you did not hear it, were sick, or did not understand  then it was just too bad, there was not any way of getting the information. So, you just had to hope that you understod everything correctly and that you had all the important things in your notes from the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Diplomatic and consular law, Private International law, Comparative law, Self-determination and minority rights, negotiations skills, legal aspects of real estate transactions.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiations skills, legal aspects of real estate transactions, Self-determination and minority rights.

questions.answer: None, I thought it was fun to expirience something new.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the openess

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Esade is okay, but you should not expect to receive a lot of help. Don't take the course Private International law, because there is Spanish laws and legislation, even tough it does not say so, and the uni will ask you to google translate it on your own... It is very different because it is a private university.

questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Getting friends from other countries and to get out of your comfort zone.

questions.answer: The Private International law course, where they wanted me to google translate Spanish law and legislation without any Spanish knowledge.
